newsitem.title: USA: Ore. consumers protest PGE, Enron merger.
newsitem.headline: Ore. consumers protest PGE, Enron merger.

text.p: Eight Oregon-based consumer advocacy and utility groups filed a joint protest of the proposed merger of Portland General Electric Co (PGE) and Enron Corp.
A spokesman at the Oregon Pubic Utilities Commission (OPUC) in Salem said Tuesday staff had not begun to tackle the huge volume of documents filed Monday by the consumer groups.
This latest group of protestors include Community Action Directors of Oregon, Citizens' Utility Board of Oregon and Oregon Committee for Equitable Utility rates.

The joint filing argues that Enron's application to acquire PGE fails to provide safeguards to Oregon ratepayers and asks the OPUC to require unbundling PGE's rates as a condition of the deal, the groups said in a release.
Enron and PGE said last week they would submit a plan to the OPUC to open PGE's service territory to competition from other power suppliers within 60 days of the merger's approval.

The plan included a proposal to separate PGE's generating facilities from its transmission and distribution system, a move Enron officials had previously ruled out pending restructuring of the state's entire electricity market.
But the consumer groups insist the merger should provide concrete benefits to customers, and not just demonstrate a lack of harm to the public interest.
Other aspects of the deal, including issues of market power and dominance of regional electricity transmission systems, have also been formally questioned by other western utilities.
Houston-based Enron and Portland General announced in July a plan to merge via a tax-free stock-for-stock deal valued near $2.1 billion.
Shareholders of both firms have approved the deal, but it must still be approved by the OPUC as well as the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission.
